title: AlgoTrace common definitions v2
description: Definitions shared by all AlgoTrace schemas of major version 2. Not a record type of its own.

schema_version.description: Version of the schema the record follows: major.minor. A minor version only adds optional fields, so every 2.x record is valid against the newest 2.x schema.

timestamp.description: UTC time, ISO 8601 with milliseconds and Z.

run_id.description: First 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (RFC 8785) of {series_id, config_sha256, model_key, instance_id, repetition, run_attempt}. Every attempt of a run has its own run_id and its own log file (protocol run-settings.md, section 6).

run_attempt.description: Number of the attempt of a run (same series_id, model_key, instance_id and repetition) from 1; a run that ended with api_error is repeated from the start as the next attempt (protocol run-settings.md, section 6).

relative_path.description: Path relative to the repository root, with forward slashes, never absolute.

env_var_name.description: Name of an environment variable that holds a secret. The secret itself never appears in any file.

provider.description: API provider; names follow OpenTelemetry gen_ai.provider.name where it has one. openai_compatible = another server with the OpenAI Chat Completions API.

condition.description: Experimental condition (protocol design.md): main = without injected faults, faults = fault injection (D02). The stage of the study and the variant of the texts are separate fields (series, prompt_variant), because pilot variants combine with both conditions.

series.description: Stage of the study (protocol design.md, section 3): pilot or full. A stage has several configurations, each with its own series_id (one per condition, fault type or pilot group) and one instance file.

prompt_variant.description: Variant of the texts for the model (protocol prompts.md, section 10). main = the texts of the full study; the others are pilot groups: no_announcement = without the request to announce the algorithm (D01), para_order, para_names, para_wording = paraphrases, hanoi_state = move returns the pegs (D08), compare_symbols = compare returns < or >.

optional_count.description: A count the provider may not report (null).

sort_state.description: Sorting: the hidden array, distinct integers (the study uses permutations of 1..N).

hanoi_state.description: Towers of Hanoi: three pegs, each a list of disk sizes from bottom to top (disks numbered from 1, the smallest).

search_state.description: Search: the hidden sorted array and the target value given in the task description.

state.description: Full hidden state of the environment, by task family.

usage.description: Token usage in the provider's own counts; null = not reported. input includes cached_input; output includes reasoning when the provider counts it so.

price.description: Price list entry of one model (the paid plan, also for a model used on a free plan) with its date and source; cost = ((input - cached_input) * input_per_mtok + cached_input * cached_input_per_mtok + cache_write * cache_write_per_mtok + output * output_per_mtok) / 1e6, a null count as 0.

optional_cost.description: Nominal cost (protocol run-settings.md, section 7); null when the price is null (a local model, counted as 0 by the budget guard).

fault_type.description: Injected tool fault (protocol fault-injection.md, section 4): one_off = the c-th valid call fails once; persistent = the c-th valid call and the next valid calls of the same tool fail, fault_length calls in total.

fault_schedule.description: Schedule of the injected fault of one instance, drawn once before the series (protocol fault-injection.md, section 3): fault_seed = base_fault_seed + idx, fault_position = c, the number of the valid call other than done that gets the fault (calls rejected by validation do not count). The same for every model and both fault types.

secret_free_object.description: Provider-specific parameters as sent; keys that usually carry a secret are not allowed.

timeouts.description: Time limits of one model (protocol run-settings.md, section 5): request_timeout_s per attempt of one request (exceeding it is a retried error), run_timeout_s per run without the pauses for a provider's daily limit (exceeding it ends the run with time_limit). The protocol uses 300 s and 3 h in the cloud, 600 s and 6 h locally.

run_limits.description: Limits of one run: max_steps from the size, the error, reminder, token and cost limits from the series, the time limits from the model. A tool call with a validation error or an injected fault is a step; a skipped call is not.

validation_error.description: Why the environment rejected a tool call (it is not executed and the state does not change); checked in this order (protocol prompts.md, section 9): after_done, unknown_tool, bad_arguments, out_of_range, same_index, illegal_move. Several calls in one turn are allowed (protocol D04 A), so there is no error for an extra call; calls after done in the same turn get after_done.

validation_detail.description: Detail of illegal_move (protocol prompts.md, section 9): empty_peg = the source peg has no disks, larger_on_smaller = a disk onto a smaller one, same_peg = from_peg equals to_peg.

skipped_reason.description: Why a call of the last turn was not processed (protocol run-settings.md, sections 3 and 8): the run ended at step_limit or too_many_errors on an earlier call of the same turn. A skipped call is not a step.

end_reason.description: Why the run ended (closed list of the protocol, run-settings.md section 8).

finish_reason.description: Normalized reason why the model stopped generating; the provider's own value goes to finish_reason_raw.
